title: Can you Survive?
author: explocion200
selftext:
So I love RTS games. I like to think I’m even good at them, so I went ahead and started making my own. It’s kind of a medieval spin on a game called Million Lords I used to play. I made sure it’s not pay to win, and now I’m not even the top dog in my own game!

Players have joined and they’re so hardcore I’ve been getting demolished. Maybe I’m just not as good as I thought. I’ll just stick to improving the game and fighting on the sidelines while the big dogs battle it out.

Anyways, if you want to see if you could survive, come join the medieval slaughter at [playcrownlands.com](http://playcrownlands.com)

comments.author: BytefailVS
comments.body: I was the other crownlands dev on itch. I ended up stopping development once I found your title. Turns out we had a similar idea and you were further along than I was. I was going for a neopet inspired kingdom growth online browser game also called crownlands (ai came up with the name) The funny part is a lot of the names that you used are clearly baked as default fantasy names used by gpt. The big reason I stopped was I went and asked myself what does my game offer that's different from everything else out there. Turns out not a whole lot, other than I made it myself with the blueprints of others that inspired it came before. Ai can create an amazing platform for your game ideas but making it fun for real players is a whole other challenge.

replies.author: explocion200
replies.body: I 100% agree. I've found myself looking at other games for inspiration, even tried a near clone of Million Lords, and realized it had the same paywalls and the same feel. That defeats the purpose of working on my own project. What started as a hobby and a handful of players is growing with all the feedback into something that feels more unique, while i play i see endless things that need to change or players tell me features they want to see in the game. Honestly after all the headaches , time , money and endless gpt prompts its shaping out to he something unique. I'd love to hear your ideas or lessons learned, even ones you had to set aside. If you're open to it, I'd really welcome your perspective on what could make this game stand on its own, not just echo what's already out there. Im sure you had a million ideas that weren't implemented. Maybe one of those is the bread and butter of something awesome. Here's the link to the discord if you ever have the time. https://discord.gg/v6K8z6day
